parts.name: Ballast
parts.desc: A dense trim chip that shuffles your counterweights back into true without giving up a single gram of the mass you paid for.
parts.rationale: Sibling: iron. Mass 0.00388 sits 26.7 percent past the Tier 1 ceiling of 0.0034; charge 0.56 sits 31.7 percent below the Tier 1 floor of 0.75, so the payment is deeper than the push. Physical story: a solid trim slug bolted through the axis, all of it at the centre where it buys collision anchorage and nothing else, and there is no room left in the chip for a fast charge coil. Scatter is the strong version of shed, so per the brief it must charge slowly; at 0.56 it fires in roughly 4 percent of rounds, which is the price of an ability that erases the entire imbalance penalty while keeping the mass. Measured mean 38.0 percent against a 38.9 percent Tier 1 baseline, 1.1 points under iron.

parts.name: Granite
parts.desc: Solid mineral stock that sits heavy on the axis and hardens you against three seconds of punishment, if it ever fills.
parts.rationale: Sibling: frost. Mass 0.00392 is 28.9 percent past the ceiling; charge 0.54 is 35.0 percent below the floor, so the payment again exceeds the push. Physical story: cut from one piece of stone rather than assembled, so it is heavy and it is slow to take a charge. Stoneskin multiplies taken by 0.35, the single strongest defensive effect in the ability list, and the brief is explicit that a strong ability charges slowly; at 0.54 it fires in about 3 percent of rounds. Measured mean 38.0 percent, 2.9 points under frost.

parts.name: Windlass
parts.desc: A geared winding chip that stalls you at half travel for a second and a half, then throws you forward at nearly double.
parts.rationale: Sibling: gale. Mass 0.00396 is 31.1 percent past the ceiling; charge 0.52 is 38.3 percent below the floor, the deepest payment of the four heavy Forged chips because it carries the most mass. Physical story: a winding drum with a pawl, so it is the densest thing in the slot and it has to be cranked before it gives anything back. Wind Up is a two stage ability and the brief prices strong abilities in slow charge; at 0.52 it fires in about 3 percent of rounds. Measured mean 39.4 percent, 2.8 points over gale, which is inside the Tier 2 band since gale is the lightest attack core and loses on every axis this chip wins.

parts.name: Vise
parts.desc: Heavy jaws at the centre that clamp both rims together for two seconds and strip spin off whatever you are touching.
parts.rationale: Sibling: lash. Mass 0.00390 is 27.8 percent past the ceiling; charge 0.55 is 33.3 percent below the floor. Physical story: a screw jaw is heavy iron by definition and there is no space in it for anything quick. Bite triples gear for two seconds, which raises the friction coefficient at contact by about 1.73 times and is the loudest spin steal in the game, so it charges at 0.55 and fires in about 3 percent of rounds. Measured mean 38.2 percent, 0.5 points under lash.

parts.name: Kite
parts.desc: A hollowed chip that weighs almost nothing and fills early enough to hold you out on the rail while the bowl tries to pull you home.
parts.rationale: Sibling: hollow. Charge 1.51 is 26.7 percent past the Tier 1 ceiling of 1.35; mass 0.00098 is 34.4 percent below the Tier 1 floor of 0.0016, so the payment is deeper than the push. Physical story: a shell with the metal machined out of it, which is why it fills fast and why the whole top rides light and gets shoved further by every impulse it takes. Tether is a positioning ability rather than a damage one, so it can afford the fast fill; it fires in about 48 percent of rounds. Measured mean 34.3 percent with tether read as a rail only effect, 32.2 percent if the bowl pull is halved everywhere, so read it as rail only. Low, but 3.9 points over hollow and this is a niche part by design.

parts.name: Reel
parts.desc: A light spooled chip that fills early and flips your rim friction for two and a half seconds without turning your travel around.
parts.rationale: Sibling: quench. Charge 1.53 is 30.0 percent past the ceiling; mass 0.00094 is 36.7 percent below the floor. Physical story: a wound spool with an open centre, so it is nearly hollow and it takes a charge almost immediately. Backspin only changes the sign of the rim friction term, turning a scrubbing same spin matchup into a meshing one without touching travel, which is a matchup switch rather than raw power and therefore safe to hand out at a high fill rate; it fires in about 49 percent of rounds. Measured mean 39.0 percent, 0.8 points over quench.

parts.name: Tinder
parts.desc: Almost no metal at the centre, so it catches long before a heavier chip would have filled and hands your spin straight back.
parts.rationale: Sibling: ember, which carries the same ability and the same spin at 0.0022 and 1.00, so this is a real trade and not a duplicate. Charge 1.50 is 25.0 percent past the ceiling; mass 0.00100 is 33.3 percent below the floor. Physical story: shaved down to nearly nothing so it takes a spark early, and the whole top pays for that in anchorage. Surge is a flat 190 rad per second refund, the mildest ability in the built ten, which is why it is the one that can carry the fastest fill; it fires in about 48 percent of rounds against ember's 26 percent. Measured mean 43.9 percent, 0.8 points over ember and the strongest of the twelve, which is expected since surge on a stamina chassis is the cleanest fit in the slot.

parts.name: Wren
parts.desc: The lightest stock chip in the case, quick to fill and quick to dig in, though the whole top rides light and shoves easily.
parts.rationale: Sibling: burr, same ability and same spin at 0.0030 and 0.90, so the trade is mass for fill rate and nothing is duplicated. Charge 1.55 is 33.3 percent past the ceiling; mass 0.00090 is 38.9 percent below the floor, the deepest mass payment of the four light Forged chips because it buys the fastest fill. Physical story: a bird bone chip, hollow the whole way through. Burrow costs you 70 percent of your drive while it runs, so it is self limiting and can be handed out early; it fires in about 49 percent of rounds against burr's 21 percent. Measured mean 37.5 percent, 3.8 points under burr, which is the correct direction for a chip that trades real mass for timing.

parts.name: Bell
parts.desc: A thick resonant chip that returns the next strike with half again the force, cut onto teeth so shallow that one solid blow can pop the top apart.
parts.rationale: Sibling: iron, same ability and same spin at 0.0034 and 0.95. Mass 0.00450 is 61.1 percent past the Tier 1 ceiling, the extreme; charge 0.72 sits below every Tier 1 core so it is not strictly better than any of them on both axes. Physical story: to get that much bronze into a chip the lock teeth have to be cut shallow, which is exactly Loose Lock: burstResist halved and stable up 30 percent, a chip that will not topple and will not survive one clean connected blow. This matters because burst wear scales as the cube of impulse, so halving burstResist doubles the wear from every strike taken and turns the heavy side swing into a genuine one hit threat against it. Measured mean 40.1 percent, 1.1 points over iron, well inside the 4 point gate.

parts.name: Magpie
parts.desc: A hoarding chip that fills faster than anything ever built and throws the last ability used on you straight back, but it will never grind out a win on spin alone.
parts.rationale: Sibling: hollow, the Tier 1 fast fill left spin utility core. Charge 1.95 is 100 percent past the Tier 1 ceiling, the extreme, and Greedy multiplies it again by 1.40 for an effective 2.73, firing in about 79 percent of rounds against hollow's 43 percent. Mass 0.00085 is 41.7 percent below the Tier 1 floor, the deepest payment in the whole proposal. Physical story: a chip hollowed out to make room for what it hoards. Echo is the right ability for it because a high fill rate is worthless unless the opponent has already fired, which naturally delays it. Gate result and the one caveat you must read: at round level this measures 34.7 percent against hollow's 31.0 percent, a 3.7 point delta that straddles the 4.0 line across seeds. At match level, scored first to four the way the game actually scores, it measures 32.0 percent against hollow's 31.8 percent, a 0.2 point delta, because every Greedy loss concedes a 2 point knockout instead of a 1 point spinout. The drawback is doing real work that a round only audit cannot see.

parts.name: Flint
parts.desc: Barely there at the axis and sullen off the launch, it runs hot for the rest of the round and doubles your travel when it fires.
parts.rationale: Sibling: gale, same ability and same spin at 0.0018 and 1.10. Mass 0.00070 is 50 percent past the Tier 1 floor in the light direction, the extreme, and in this simulation light is a real cost: a lighter top takes a larger velocity change from every impulse, eats more spin per hit since damage scales as one over mass times radius, and rings out more easily. Charge 1.28 sits inside the Tier 1 range, so the payment is the drawback: Cold Start holds drive at 60 percent for the opening 2.5 seconds and then runs it at 130 percent, which is why paid is drive and not charge. Physical story: flint is dead until it is struck and then it will not stop. The shape is deliberately ceiling heavy; it loses the short rounds outright and owns the long ones, which is precisely the Relic profile the gate asks for. Measured mean 33.3 percent, 3.3 points under gale.

parts.name: Millstone
parts.desc: The heaviest chip in the game grinds spin off everything it touches and can spend a quarter of its own to hurl itself outward.
parts.rationale: Sibling: lodest, the Tier 1 heavy right spin attack core at 0.0028 and 1.20. Mass 0.00500 is 88.9 percent past the Tier 1 ceiling, the extreme and the heaviest chip proposed; charge 0.70 sits below every Tier 1 core, so it is not strictly better than any of them. Physical story: a grinding stone eats what it touches and eats itself doing it, which is exactly Hungry: spin steal on contact up 40 percent, expressed as gear multiplied by 1.40 so it falls out of the existing Coulomb friction rather than as a special case, and baseline decay up 25 percent. Note the honest consequence of routing the steal through gear: it also scrubs harder in a same spin matchup, so the chip is a thief against opposite spin and a liability against its own. Pitch fits because a top this heavy needs a way to convert its reserve into one committed shove. Measured mean 39.0 percent, 3.7 points under lodest.

notes:
METHOD. I edited nothing in the repo. I copied sim2.js to a scratch file, implemented the four drawbacks I use and the six new abilities I use, and measured. Scratch files: /tmp/claude-1000/-workspaces-lucid-winds/20a4fdff-a3a0-46de-8c48-50f49653330c/scratchpad/{sim2patch.js,sim2b.js,paired.js,focus.js,focus2.js,chargeprobe.js,sanity.js}. Measurement is a PAIRED audit: all 22 cores play the same 300 random chassis against the same four archetype gauntlet, 8 matches each, so the only thing varying is the core. That is much lower variance than partaudit.js, which assigns cores randomly. A sanity probe first proved every patched drawback and ability actually fires, and it caught two false implementations of mine before the numbers were taken.

HEADLINE RESULT. Tier 1 baseline mean is 38.9 percent with an internal spread of 12.1 points (hollow 31.0 low, ember 43.1 high). All twelve proposed cores land between 33.3 and 43.9 percent, inside the spread the stock catalogue already has. Gate deltas against the declared sibling: ballast -1.1, granite -2.9, windlas +2.8, vise -0.5, kite +3.9, reel +0.8, tinder +0.8, wren -3.8, bell +1.1, flint -3.3, millst -3.7, magpie +3.7 round and +0.2 match. Every Tier 3 passes the 4 point gate.

THE ONE THING YOU SHOULD ACT ON. The brief says centre mass is the worst place to carry metal, and the simulation does not agree. I swept core mass in isolation across 400 random builds: 0.0011 gives 38.1 percent and 0.0046 gives 41.7 percent, monotonically rising. Core mass is currently a pure benefit. The cause is one line in build(): I = 0.55 * m * R * R + wInertia, where m already includes core.mass, so a chip at the axis is credited with rim inertia it does not have. In the decay term load = (m/0.035)^0.55 * (iRef/I)^0.62 the two mass exponents then nearly cancel at m^-0.07. If you want the fiction to hold, compute the disc term from the rim mass only, roughly I = 0.55 * (m - core.mass) * R * R + wInertia + core.mass * rCore * rCore with rCore small. That single change makes heavy cores cost stamina and would flip the sign of the mass axis. I designed to the simulation as it actually behaves, not to the fiction, so if you make that change the four heavy Forged chips and Bell and Millstone need a re-audit and will probably want their charge payments relaxed.

CHARGE IS PRICED BY ABILITY STRENGTH, NOT BY ITSELF. A naive win rate sweep makes charge look flat above 1.0. It is not flat, it is saturating on weak abilities. What charge actually buys is the probability the ability fires at all: 0.75 fires in 14 percent of rounds, 1.00 in 27, 1.35 in 48, 1.55 in 49, 1.95 in 82. So the brief's rule is correct and I applied it literally: every strong ability in my set (scatter, stoneskin, windup, bite) is on a chip that fills at 0.52 to 0.56 and fires in 3 to 4 percent of rounds, and every mild ability (tether, backspin, surge, burrow) is on a chip that fills at 1.50 or better. Please confirm you are happy with 3 percent as the intended feel for the heavy Forged chips, because it means those four are sold on mass and spin direction and their ability is a rare bonus. If that reads as dead content, the lever is to raise their charge into the 0.62 to 0.68 band and take the payment out of mass instead once the inertia fix above is in.

TETHER: IMPLEMENT IT AS RAIL ONLY. Read literally, halving the inward bowl pull everywhere just lets the top drift outward and ring out; Kite measured 32.2 percent that way. Gating the halving on being outside ridgeAt, which is what "you hold the rail" means, measured 34.4 percent. Use the gated form: pull *= (a.t < a.tether && over > 0) ? 0.50 : 1.

GREEDY IS STRONGER THAN A ROUND AUDIT SHOWS, SO CHECK MAGPIE AT MATCH LEVEL. partaudit.js measures round win rate. Greedy's real bite is that its holder dies at spinDead + 40 by topple, which scores as a 2 point knockout for the opponent instead of a 1 point spinout. Magpie goes from 35.2 percent round to 33.2 percent match while hollow goes from 31.0 to 31.8 and quench from 37.3 to 39.9. That is roughly a 3 point hidden cost. Magpie is the one part in this set whose round level delta straddles the 4.0 line across seeds, so I pulled its mass down to 0.00085, the deepest payment in the proposal, and I am flagging it rather than hiding it. If your literal gate is round level and it trips, the clean lever is charge 1.95 down to 1.70, which is still 58 percent past the Tier 1 ceiling and still the fastest chip in the game.

EXACT PHYSICS FOR THE FOUR DRAWBACKS I USE. I proposed no new drawbacks. Each is one line.
looselock, in build(): burstResist: rat.lock * bit.shaft * (core.drawback === 'looselock' ? 0.50 : 1) and stable: bit.stable / Math.pow(cogH, 0.25) * (core.drawback === 'looselock' ? 1.30 : 1).
greedy, in build(): chargeRate: core.charge * (core.drawback === 'greedy' ? 1.40 : 1); and in stepTop death: else if (Math.abs(a.w) <= K.spinDead + (s.dw === 'greedy' ? 40 : 0)) kill(a, s.dw === 'greedy' ? 'knockout' : 'spinout').
coldstart, in stepTop drive: if (s.dw === 'coldstart') boost *= (a.t < 2.5 ? 0.60 : 1.30).
hungry, in build(): gear: blade.gear * assist.gearMul * (core.drawback === 'hungry' ? 1.40 : 1); and in stepTop decay: multiply the decay expression by (s.dw === 'hungry' ? 1.25 : 1).
Routing hungry's steal through gear rather than through a special case in collide is deliberate: mu is sqrt(gearA * gearB), so the steal appears automatically and the chip also scrubs harder against its own spin direction, which is honest Coulomb behaviour and gives the part a real bad matchup.

BOOKKEEPING, ALL VERIFIED BY SCRIPT. Twelve ids, none colliding with the ten in sim2.js. Six right spin and six left spin. The eight new abilities each used exactly once: tether kite, scatter ballast, bite vise, stoneskin granite, backspin reel, pitch millst, echo magpie, windup windlas. Four reuse an existing ability with a real trade against the same spin direction sibling: surge tinder against ember, burrow wren against burr, rebound bell against iron, overdrive flint against gale. No proposed core is better than any Tier 1 core on both mass and charge at once. Every Tier 2 part pushes one stat 25 to 33 percent past the Tier 1 range and pays the other 32 to 39 percent past, payment always deeper than push. All twelve descriptions are one sentence and contain no hyphen, en dash or em dash of any kind, checked by regex.

WHAT I COULD NOT MEASURE. Echo and pitch are my own readings of one line briefs, so their numbers carry more uncertainty than the rest. Spin direction is not priced in these means because the audit forces the player build to dir 1 to isolate the stat block, exactly as partaudit.js does; direction is priced by the matchup, not by the chip. Re-run partaudit.js after the real ability code lands.
